clue.text: See 2
Ascendant team man joining party — one of those having a big bash?

definitions.text: one of those having a big bash?

indicators.note: in a down clue ascendant should mean written upwards, but upwards the team gives the wrong order, so it can only work as a loose signal to rearrange

parts.note: a crew is a team
a king is a man in chess
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A team member joins a party, apparently one of the revellers at a big bash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascendant' surely meant CREW written upwards, but that gives WERC, not WREC: the blog and its commenters call it Paul's slip, so only a jumbling reading fits. 'bash' means a blow, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A demolition crane swings its heavy weight to smash buildings, so it is something dealing a big blow.

clue.text: See 20
Charges are almost entirely in rags when labouring

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the word are loses its final letter
labouring means working hard, so the letters of in and rags are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone almost entirely in rags is charged while doing hard labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' trims ARE to AR; 'when labouring' rearranges IN and RAGS into RAIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to formally accuse them in court, so it means charges as a verb.

clue.text: Area offering cold bath with undies off?

definitions.text: Area offering cold bath with undies off?

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A place where you can take a chilly dip after removing your underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of C, BATH and UNDIES; the whole clue also describes the place, where swimming in a chilly sea without underwear is normal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of seaside set aside for naked bathing offers a cold swim with no clothing at all.

clue.text: See 12 across
Emperor tricked, laughing briefly

parts.note: to be had is to be tricked or fooled

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for laughing is dropped

parts.note: riant is a literary word, from French, for laughing or cheerful

explanation.surface: An emperor is fooled while laughing for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens RIANT, a rare word for laughing, to RIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman ruler of the second century, famous for the wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Felon goes round licking small fried item

indicators.note: the convict's word surrounds the other piece, so it is put inside

parts.note: a con is a convict, a felon
a licking is a heavy defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: A criminal takes a beating while going round a small fried snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licking' looks like eating but means a thrashing; 'goes round' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a little cube of fried bread scattered on soup or salad.

clue.text: International alliance building legacy of co-operation, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the four words that follow it

explanation.surface: An international alliance builds a legacy of co-operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'building legacy of co-operation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations united by a common interest, such as a trading or military pact.

clue.text: Mockery made of shortcoming when opener dismissed

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and dismissed means sent away, as an opening batsman is in cricket

parts.note: a limitation is a shortcoming or weakness

explanation.surface: A mockery is made of a team's weakness when its opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when opener dismissed' removes the first letter L, with a nod to a cricket opener being out.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation can be a mockery: a poor copy or parody of the real thing.

clue.text: Asian country incomplete? Thailand once unfinished

parts.note: read cryptically, in-complete is IN plus DONE, complete meaning done; the question mark admits the trick

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is left off the old name

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: An Asian country is described as incomplete, as Thailand once was unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete?' is split as in-complete, and complete means done. 'unfinished' drops the last letter of Thailand's old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is the island republic of South-East Asia, home to Java and Sumatra.

clue.text: Elicit cheers, as might a 2 1?

definitions.meaning: a performer who ... the house ... wins rapturous applause
a wrecking ball, the answer to 2 and 1 ..., literally knocks a house to the ground

explanation.surface: A performance is so good it earns applause, the way a demolition tool would.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition points at the linked answer at 2 and 1 down, WRECKING BALL, which literally demolishes a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to win overwhelming applause; the literal sense is demolishing a building.

clue.text: See 5
Write in figures like 1, first of scores in match

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
the figure one gives I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: in places the first letter of scores inside the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of scores

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a score like 1 in numbers within a match report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes S from 'scores', and 'in' puts it inside TIE, a cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: To digitise is to convert into digital form, recording information as numbers.

clue.text: Persuasive conversation turning stale, developer of vaccine has admitted

indicators.note: the vaccine developer's name takes in, or lets inside, the other letters

parts.note: Jonas Salk developed the first successful polio vaccine

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters of stale are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conversation goes stale when it turns to someone who admits to developing a vaccine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the letters of 'stale' and 'has admitted' places them inside the surname of the polio vaccine pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales pitch is persuasive talk aimed at getting someone to buy.

clue.text: Rear pinched in dance — smack!

indicators.note: pinched means stolen, so the rear, or last letter, of the dance is taken away

parts.note: the tango is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: Someone's bottom is pinched during a dance, earning a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear pinched' looks like a groping; it takes the last letter O off TANGO. 'smack' means flavour, not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack of something is a distinct taste of it, just as a tang is a sharp flavour.

clue.text: Long time in that Midwest state

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Someone has lived a long time in a particular state of the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long while, as in not seen you for ages.

clue.text: King has stopped uprising in besieged city, private location of US siege

indicators.note: the king's letter stops, or plugs, a gap in the reversed city
in a down clue, uprising means the city's name is written upwards

parts.note: Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years
K is the chess abbreviation for king
own means private, as in your own room

explanation.surface: A king blocks a rising in a besieged city, a private place in an American siege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TROY into YORT, and 'has stopped' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorktown in Virginia was where the British army surrendered after a siege in 1781.

clue.text: See 14
See 12 across
Old picture in ecclesiastical books primarily found in ordinals

indicators.note: these letters are found inside the word for ordinals, placed within it

parts.note: thirds are ordinal numbers, as in first, second and third

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letters of ecclesiastical and books

explanation.surface: An old painting is found in church books, catalogued by number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives E and B, which 'found in' puts inside THIRDS. 'picture' means film here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birds is Alfred Hitchcock's 1963 thriller, an old movie or picture.

clue.text: Where own reflection might appear furious

definitions.meaning: literally, a reflection of you appears ... you, next to your own self

explanation.surface: Seeing your own reflection makes you angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a reflection, in a window say, sits right beside you.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means out of control with emotion, usually anger or distress.

clue.text: Praise line penned by Elizabeth

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the line is placed inside the name

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth writes a line of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like writing but means enclosing: L goes inside BESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless God is to praise or glorify Him, as in hymns and prayers.

clue.text: The making of a Brazilian football team inspired by a win surprisingly in another sporting activity?

indicators.note: in places the whole team-and-win group inside the sport

parts.note: biking, or cycling, is a sport

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the team's letters are taken inside the rearranged win
surprisingly signals the letters of a win come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: XI, eleven players, is a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A Brazilian football team, inspired by a surprise win, takes up another sporting activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns 'a win' into IWAN; 'inspired by' puts the team inside it, giving IWAXIN, and 'in' puts that inside the cycling word. A Brazilian is a full intimate wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian is a style of wax removing almost all pubic hair, so a bikini wax creates one.

clue.text: Stuffing knocked out in four attacks at sea, move on quickly

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
with its stuffing, or inside, knocked out, only the outer letters of four are left

explanation.surface: Four attacks at sea knock the stuffing out of a fleet, which moves on quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing knocked out in' leaves FR from FOUR; 'at sea' rearranges FR with ATTACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast-track something is to push it through ahead of the usual pace.

clue.text: Chaotic worsening situation in underwater system, everything beyond belief, ultimately

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the reef and the rest follow the letter of belief
ultimately points to the final letter of belief

parts.note: a reef is an underwater ridge of rock or coral
all means everything

explanation.surface: A disastrous slide in an underwater ecosystem, where everything is ultimately beyond belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaotic' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the definition. 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'belief', and 'beyond' sets the rest after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is an uncontrolled plunge, used of markets or fortunes sliding fast with nothing to stop them.

clue.text: German composer either pianissimo ___ ?

parts.note: either pairs with or, as in either this or that
the blank asks for the opposite of pianissimo (pp), which is fortissimo, FF

explanation.surface: A musician asks whether a German composer's piece should be played very softly or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer fills the blank: 'either pianissimo OR FF', FF meaning fortissimo, very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German who wrote Carmina Burana.

clue.text: See 21
Dance note

definitions.meaning: to get something down is to note it, write it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to dance with abandon and to write something down.

clue.text: See 19
